## ⚠️ Before you update

- **Update every paired device.** This version stores subcategories, so its data is a newer version. Sync only works between devices on the same version: until all your paired devices have updated, they won't sync with each other.
- **There's no going back to 2.6.0.** The first time 2.7.0 opens, it upgrades your data. An older version can't open it afterwards, or import a backup made by 2.7.0. Your entries, totals and charts stay exactly as they were.

## 🗂️ Subcategories

Put categories under a category, such as **Fuel**, **Taxi** and **Parking** under **Transport** (#29).

- **Settings → Categories** has a **Parent category** field. It's one level deep: a subcategory has no subcategories of its own, and it takes its parent's type.
- In the new-entry and recurring forms, the list shows the main categories. Pick one with subcategories and they slide in as chips underneath, **All Transport** first.
- A main category counts its subcategories everywhere: its **budget**, the **Activity filter** and the **By category** chart, which shows main categories only.
- Deleting a subcategory moves its entries and recurring items to its parent. Deleting a main category makes its subcategories main categories.
- New installs start with 15: Fuel, Taxi, Parking and Car Maintenance under Transport; Rent and Home Maintenance under Housing; Electricity, Water, Internet and Phone under Utilities; Doctor and Pharmacy under Health; Clothes and Electronics under Shopping; Bonus under Salary. Your existing categories stay as they are.
- Voice entry files *"uber"* or *"petrol"* under Taxi or Fuel when you have them.
- The categories CSV has a `parent` column, and backups keep the tree.

## 🎨 App styles

**Settings → Appearance** (new) dresses the whole app in one of five looks: **Plain**, the indigo look and still the default, or **Leather wallet**, **Coin nap**, **Pocket LCD** and **Receipt**. Each has its own cards: stitched leather, coins pressed in at the bottom, an ink-ruled LCD box, paper torn off the roll. New installs pick one on the welcome screens. Light, Dark and Black stay with Plain.

## 🧱 Balance widgets (Android)

Two new home-screen widgets: **Overview** (your total balance, and what you spent on a day) and **Account balance** (one account, picked the first time you tap it). They and the quick add widget come in the same five styles, set in **Settings → Appearance → Widget style**. They show ••• unless **Settings → Amounts on widgets** is on, and tapping one opens the app through the lock.

## 📅 Recurring calendar

**Recurring** gets an **Items | Calendar** switch. The calendar marks what's due each day (recurring items, loan due dates and savings circle rounds), lists the picked day's items, and adds up what's still to come in and go out this month. An **Overdue** list keeps late loans and unpaid rounds in sight until they're settled.

## Improvements

- **Add from Home:** on a phone, **+ Add** and 🎤 now sit at the bottom of Home too, not only on Activity (#32).
- **Activity filters:** pick a **category**, **merchant** or **account** from a list. They combine with each other and with search.
- **100 currencies:** 31 more, including LKR (#28), NPR, KZT, GEL, ETB, GHS and DOP.
- **E-Wallet** accounts, a fifth account type.
- **Unencrypted backups:** Export Backup asks whether to encrypt the file. Encryption stays the recommended default; **Don't encrypt** saves plain JSON you can read with your own tools. Automatic backups are always encrypted. The file formats are documented in [`docs/formats.md`](https://github.com/software-ace/PocketSense/blob/v2.7.0/docs/formats.md) (#27).

## Fixes

- A budget can be deleted on a phone: swipe it away, or tap it and choose **Delete** (#30).
- On narrow phones, **Transfer** and **New account** stack instead of wrapping **New account** onto two lines (#31).

## Download
**Android**
- Also on **[F-Droid](https://f-droid.org/packages/ace.software.pocketsense/)**, which keeps it updated. It ships these same signed APKs, so you can switch between the two and keep your data.
- **`PocketSense-v2.7.0-arm64-v8a.apk`**: almost all modern Android phones. Use this one if unsure.
- `PocketSense-v2.7.0-armeabi-v7a.apk`: older 32-bit phones
- `PocketSense-v2.7.0-x86_64.apk`: emulators and Chromebooks

Installs as an update over any earlier version and keeps your data.

**Windows 10 or 11 (x64)**: pick one.
- **`PocketSense-v2.7.0-windows-x64-setup.exe`**: run it. It installs just for you without admin rights, or for everyone if you choose.
- `PocketSense-v2.7.0-windows-x64.msi`: installs for everyone on the PC, for example when deploying it across an organization.
- `PocketSense-v2.7.0-windows-x64.zip`: unpack it anywhere and run `pocket_sense.exe`.

**Linux (x86_64)**: pick one.
- **Debian, Ubuntu, Mint:** `PocketSense-v2.7.0-linux-x64.deb`
  ```sh
  sudo apt install ./PocketSense-v2.7.0-linux-x64.deb
  ```
- **Fedora, openSUSE:** `PocketSense-v2.7.0-linux-x64.rpm`
  ```sh
  sudo dnf install ./PocketSense-v2.7.0-linux-x64.rpm   # or: sudo zypper install
  ```
- **Any distro:** `PocketSense-v2.7.0-x86_64.AppImage`. Make it executable and run it.
- **Any distro:** `PocketSense-v2.7.0-linux-x64.tar.gz`. Unpack it and run `./PocketSense/pocket_sense`.

All need glibc 2.35 or newer, and a running keyring (GNOME Keyring or KWallet) or a passphrase. With the AppImage or the tarball you also need GTK 3, and `parecord` for voice entry (`pulseaudio-utils` on Debian/Ubuntu/Fedora, `libpulse` on Arch).
